speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific episodes of unresponsiveness you are experiencing, including how long they last and what triggers them. Have you noticed any specific behaviors, like facial grimacing or lip smacking, during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (Evolution from Childhood Absence Seizures).

The patient's history of staring spells evolving into prolonged unresponsiveness with post-ictal lethargy and automatisms (hand gestures) is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the duration of 3–4 minutes and the prolonged confusion afterwards, he is not in a typical brief absence seizure but rather a specific type of non-convulsive status epilepticus. I will not ask further questions as the clinical picture is definitive; immediate EEG confirmation is required. REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram). REQUEST IMAGES: EEG_Trace.
